The righteous fulfill vows, fear a dreadful Day and feed the needy, orphan and captive only for Allah, who protects them and rewards their patience with a garden and silk.
In Paradise they recline on couches in shade with neither sun nor cold, served silver vessels and ginger-mixed drink by eternal youths, wearing green silk and silver bracelets.
Having sent down the Quran progressively, Allah tells the Prophet to be patient, not obey sinners, and remember his Lord's name morning, evening and long into the night.
Disbelievers love the fleeting life, though Allah made them and can change them; this is a reminder, yet none wills unless Allah wills; He admits whom He wills to mercy.
By the winds and the message-bringing angels, what is promised will happen: stars are obliterated, the heaven opens, mountains are blown away, and woe that Day to the deniers.
Allah destroyed the former peoples and will follow them with the later ones; thus He deals with criminals, and woe that Day to the deniers.
Allah created people from a disdained fluid placed in a firm lodging for a known term; woe that Day to the deniers.
Allah made the earth a container for the living and the dead, set lofty mountains and gave sweet water to drink; woe that Day to the deniers.
Deniers will be sent to a three-columned shadow of smoke giving no shade from the flame, which throws sparks as huge as fortresses.
On the Day of Judgement the deniers will not speak or be allowed excuses; all peoples are assembled, and they are challenged to plan against Allah if they can.
The righteous will be among shade, springs and fruits they desire, told to eat and drink in satisfaction for what they did, as Allah rewards the doers of good.
The criminals may eat and enjoy briefly; they refuse to bow when told, and are asked in what statement after the Quran they will believe.
People question one another about the great news, the Day of Judgement, over which they disagree; they will soon come to know.
Allah made the earth a resting place, mountains as stakes, people in pairs, sleep for rest, night and day, seven heavens, a burning lamp, and rain for grain and gardens.
The Day of Judgement is appointed: the Horn is blown, people come in multitudes, the heaven opens into gateways and the mountains become a mirage.
Hell lies in wait for transgressors, who will stay for ages tasting only scalding water and purulence, a fit recompense for denying the account and Allah's verses.
The righteous attain gardens, grapevines, companions of equal age and a full cup, hearing no ill speech or falsehood, a reward and gift from their Lord.
On the True Day the Spirit and angels stand in rows, none speaking without permission; each will see what he sent ahead, and the disbeliever will wish he were dust.
By the angels who take souls and arrange affairs, on the Day of the blast and the one that follows, hearts will tremble and eyes be humbled.
They ask whether they will be returned to life after becoming decayed bones, calling it a losing return, yet one shout will bring them onto the earth's surface.
Allah called Moses in the valley of Tuwa to go to transgressing Pharaoh, who denied the great sign, proclaimed himself most exalted lord, and was seized in exemplary punishment.
Allah built the heaven, raised it, darkened its night and brought out its brightness, then spread the earth, brought out its water and pasture and set the mountains as provision.
When the great Calamity comes and Hellfire is exposed, whoever transgressed and preferred worldly life goes to Hellfire, and whoever feared his Lord and restrained his desires goes to Paradise.
They ask the Prophet when the Hour comes; its time rests with his Lord, he is only a warner, and they will feel they stayed but an afternoon or morning.
The Prophet frowned and turned from a blind man, Ibn Umm Maktum, who came seeking purification, while attending to one who thought himself without need.
These verses are a reminder for whoever wills, recorded in honored, purified sheets carried by noble, dutiful messenger-angels.
Man is cursed for disbelief; Allah created him from a sperm-drop, eased his way, causes his death and burial and will raise him, yet he has not fulfilled His command.
Man should consider his food: Allah pours rain, splits the earth and grows grain, grapes, olives, palms, gardens, fruit and grass for people and their livestock.
When the Deafening Blast comes, a man flees from his brother, parents, wife and children; some faces will be bright and joyful, others dark with dust, the disbelievers.
When the sun is darkened, stars fall, seas are aflame, the buried girl is asked why she was killed, Hellfire blazes and Paradise nears, each soul knows what it brought.
The Quran is a noble messenger's word, not an expelled devil's; their companion, who saw Gabriel, is not mad; it is a reminder to the worlds for whoever wills.
When the sky breaks apart, stars scatter, seas erupt and graves are overturned, each soul will know what it sent forth and kept back.
Man is asked what deceived him about his Generous Lord, who created, proportioned and balanced him and assembled him in whatever form He willed.
People deny the Recompense, though noble keepers are appointed over them, recording and knowing whatever they do.
The righteous will be in pleasure and the wicked in Hellfire, burning there on the Day of Recompense and never absent from it.
The Day of Recompense is when no soul can do anything for another, and the command that Day is entirely Allah's.
Woe to those who take full measure from people but give less by measure or weight, as if they will not be resurrected before the Lord of the worlds.
The record of the wicked is in sijjeen; woe to those who deny the Day of Recompense and call Allah's verses legends; their hearts are stained, and they will burn.
The record of the righteous is in 'illiyyun; they recline on couches, faces radiant, drinking sealed wine ending in musk, mixed from Tasneem, the spring of those brought near.
Criminals used to laugh and wink at the believers and call them lost; on that Day the believers, on couches, will laugh at the disbelievers.
